name: Question 8
problem:
Suppose $n=4i+2j-8,$ where $i,j\in Z.$ Complete the following argument.

The number $n$ is {{field-1}} since 

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =4i+2j-8 \\  & =2({{field-2}}-4) \\  & ={{field-3}},\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=${{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
An integer is *even* if it can be written as $2a,$ where $a$ is an integer.

Notice that all terms in the expression $4i+2j-8$ have a common factor of $2.$ 

Therefore, we complete our argument as follows:

The number $n$ is $\text{even}$ since

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =4i+2j-8 \\  & =2({{2i+j-4}_{⏟}}_{a}) \\  & =2a,\end{aligned}
$$

where $a=2i+j-4\in Z.$
